page: Amazon Web Services d2.xlarge is a dense-storage instance belonging to the D2 family, architected primarily for workloads requiring substantial on-instance disk capacity. The configuration supplies 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 Haswell processor running at 2.4 GHz, backed by 30 MB of Level 3 cache. Memory allocation totals 30.0 GB of RAM, offering 7.62 GB per physical core. For high-density local persistence, the instance is provisioned with 6144 GB of attached hard disk drive (HDD) storage, supported by a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Hardware virtualization is mediated through the Xen hypervisor, and no graphics accelerators are present.

Benchmark outcomes reflect the architectural age of the underlying Intel Haswell processor family. Raw compute measurements through stress-ng place both single-core (738.49) and multi-core (2077.66) performance in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems. Geekbench metrics align with these results, logging single-core and multi-core scores of 890.0 and 1880.0 respectively. PassMark testing records a CPU aggregate of 3067.56 and a database operations score of 1226.13. Uncached memory read bandwidth tests out at 26.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 16.66 GB/sec. The instance executes Redis SET workloads at 1.25 million operations per second and demonstrates small-model language prompt processing at 239.51 tokens per second.

From an operational tradeoff perspective, the d2.xlarge prioritizes physical disk capacity over compute efficiency and input/output latency. The bundled 6 TB HDD array provides high sequential data density without relying on external network-attached volumes, but it lacks the random access performance of solid-state storage. CPU-intensive operations, high-frequency transactional queries, and advanced vector processing are constrained by legacy instruction support and modest per-core throughput. Consequently, the instance is cost-efficient primarily when utilized for sequential data processing pipelines, centralized log ingestion clusters, distributed data warehousing, and archival storage nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services d2.xlarge is a dense-storage instance designed for data-intensive workloads requiring large amounts of sequential disk capacity. Driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor running at 2.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 30.0 GB, paired with 6144 GB of bundled local hard disk drive storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Because of the legacy Haswell microarchitecture, CPU benchmarks such as Geekbench and stress-ng register lower compute density relative to contemporary architectures, yielding an overall profile oriented toward bulk storage over computational speed. The instance omits dedicated GPU acceleration. Given its high storage-to-compute ratio, the d2.xlarge serves workloads such as large-scale data warehousing, log processing, Apache Hadoop or Kafka nodes, and secondary archival repositories.
